rice-brown-with-carrots-and-dark-green-v.title: Brown Rice with Carrots and Dark Green Vegetables, No Added Fat

content.title: About
content.content: This dish consists of whole‑grain brown rice, sliced carrots, and dark green vegetables (such as broccoli, spinach, or green beans). It is prepared without added fats, making it a low‑calorie, nutrient‑dense option for healthy eating.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Brown rice retains the bran and germ, providing more fiber and micronutrients than white rice.
Carrots are rich in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
Dark green vegetables are excellent sources of vitamin K, folate, and antioxidants.
The dish is commonly used in weight‑loss diets because it contains no added fat.
When stored properly, brown rice can stay fresh for up to 6 months.

items.title: Supports Digestion
items.content: Fiber from whole rice and vegetables promotes intestinal motility and regular bowel movements.

items.title: Rich in Vitamins and Minerals
items.content: Provides vitamin A, vitamin K, folate, magnesium, and potassium, which are important for immunity and heart function.

items.title: Low Glycemic Index
items.content: Brown rice has a lower glycemic index than white rice, helping to stabilize blood sugar levels.

items.title: Antioxidant Protection
items.content: Beta‑carotene and other phytochemicals in carrots and green vegetables combat free radicals.

items.title: Skin Health Support
items.content: Vitamin A and antioxidants aid skin cell renewal and protect against UV damage.

items.title: Vegetable Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to certain green vegetables, such as broccoli.

items.title: Phytic Acid
items.content: Brown rice contains phytic acid, which can reduce the absorption of some minerals when consumed in excess.

items.title: Excess Beta‑Carotene
items.content: Very large amounts of carrots can cause carotenemia – a temporary yellowing of the skin.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve as a side dish with meat, fish, or tofu, toss into salads, or use as a base for nutrient‑packed bowls. Add herbs, soy sauce, or lemon juice for extra flavor if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Cool the rice completely before sealing to prevent bacterial growth.

content.title: About
content.content: Tomato and vegetable juice, 100% is a ready‑to‑drink beverage made from fresh tomatoes and a blend of vegetables such as carrots, celery, beetroot and bell pepper. The juice contains no added sugar, preservatives or flavorings and retains most of the vitamins and minerals of the raw vegetables.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomato juice is rich in lycopene, a powerful antioxidant whose availability increases with mild heating.
Combining tomatoes with carrots and beetroot enhances the bioavailability of beta‑carotene.
In Russia this juice is often used in detox programs and as a base for vegetable soups.
Pasteurisation preserves over 80% of vitamin C while extending shelf life.
Tomato juice is traditionally considered heart‑healthy because of its potassium content.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Lycopene and potassium help regulate blood pressure and reduce the risk of atherosclerosis.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Vitamin C, vitamin E and carotenoids neutralise free radicals, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Immune system boost
items.content: B‑vitamins and vitamin C support normal immune function.

items.title: Vision health
items.content: Beta‑carotene and vitamin A from carrots and tomatoes are essential for eye health.

items.title: Anti‑inflammatory effects
items.content: Phytochemicals such as polyphenols have mild anti‑inflammatory properties.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes or other vegetables in the blend.

items.title: High sodium if salt is added
items.content: When the juice contains added salt, people with hypertension should monitor their intake.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Tomato juice has a low pH, which can cause heartburn in people with acid reflux.

items.title: Natural sugar content
items.content: Although no sugar is added, the natural sugars may affect blood glucose levels in diabetics; moderation is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink the juice chilled, use it as a base for smoothies, vegetable soups or sauces. It can be diluted with water to reduce acidity. It pairs well with herbs, lemon and spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the juice in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C in a sealed container and consume within 5 days after opening. Keep away from direct sunlight and high temperatures to preserve vitamin C.

yogurt-greek-whole-milk-flavors-other-th.title: Greek Whole Milk Yogurt, Non‑Fruit Flavors

content.title: About
content.content: Greek whole‑milk yogurt is a thick, creamy dairy product made by double‑straining regular yogurt. It is flavored with non‑fruit ingredients such as vanilla, honey, caramel, or spices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Greek yogurt contains two to three times more protein than regular yogurt.
The traditional straining process removes most of the whey, giving the product its dense texture.
Non‑fruit flavors often use natural aromatics and spices, making them suitable for people with fruit allergies.
Greek yogurt is frequently used in cooking as a substitute for sour cream or mayonnaise.
In many countries Greek yogurt is considered a premium product and commands a higher price.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: A 200 g serving provides about 20 g of protein, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of probiotics
items.content: Live cultures like Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium promote gut health.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Help maintain strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Low added sugar
items.content: Non‑fruit varieties usually contain less added sugar, beneficial for blood‑glucose control.

items.title: Beneficial fats
items.content: Whole‑milk retains some milk fats, including conjugated linoleic acid (CLA) with antioxidant properties.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People who are lactose intolerant may experience discomfort.

items.title: Milk‑protein allergy
items.content: Casein and whey proteins can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Whole‑milk Greek yogurt is more caloric than low‑fat versions.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some flavored varieties may contain added salt.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy it plain, blend into smoothies, use in sauces, dips, baked goods, or as a base for desserts. Non‑fruit flavors pair well with nuts, honey, granola, and spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 1‑4 °C in the original container. Once opened, consume within 5‑7 days. Do not freeze, as texture may change.
